body.statement:
For every fixed \(t_0\in(0,1/4)\) in the witness submodel with \(\pi_0=\pi_1=1/2\), the unique surviving path satisfies \(d_H(S_s,S_t)=2|s-t|\) locally.  With the clipped estimator \(\widehat t=\min\{1/4,\max\{0,\{\widehat q_1(1,3)-\widehat q_1(1,1)\}/2\}\}\),
\[
\sqrt n\,d_H(S_{\widehat t},S_{t_0})\Rightarrow2\sqrt{1/4-2t_0^2}\,|N(0,1)|.
\]
Plug-in folded-normal quantiles give pointwise first-order Hausdorff coverage.
body.proof_tex:
For \(s,t>0\) sufficiently close to the fixed interior value \(t_0\), the common dual certificate in the metric-impossibility proof excludes the same five paths, and the surviving path gives
\[
S_t=\{(7/8,r,9/8+2t):1\le r\le1+2t\}.
\]
If \(s\ge t\), every point of \(S_t\) is matched by clamping its middle coordinate into \([1,1+2s]\), while the third coordinate moves by \(2(s-t)\); the upper endpoint of \(S_s\) attains that discrepancy.  Reversing \(s,t\) proves
\[
d_H(S_s,S_t)=2|s-t|.
\tag{1}
\]

Within arm \(Z=1\), define \(X=1/2\) on the treated cell with outcome \(2\), \(X=-1/2\) on the treated cell with outcome \(0\), and \(X=0\) otherwise.  Under \(q_{t_0}\),
\[
\mathbb EX=t_0,\qquad
\mathbb EX^2=\frac14\{(1/4+t_0)+(1/4-t_0)\}=\frac18,
\]
so \(\operatorname{Var}(X)=1/8-t_0^2\).  The characteristic-function calculation for bounded iid variables, followed by the random-arm ratio expansion, gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat t-t_0)\Rightarrow
N\!\left(0,\frac{1/8-t_0^2}{\pi_1}\right)
=N(0,1/4-2t_0^2),
\]
where the last equality uses \(\pi_1=1/2\).  Because \(t_0\) is interior, clipping changes the raw contrast with probability tending to zero.  Combining this limit with (1) and continuity of absolute value yields the displayed folded-normal law.  Replacing \(t_0\) by \(\widehat t\) in the continuous positive variance \(1/4-2t_0^2\) is consistent, so its folded-normal upper quantile yields pointwise first-order coverage.
body.justification: The solved one-path stratum verifies that the regular branch is nonvacuous and provides a calibration check and special case of the general active-germ recovery theorem.
body.gap: Generic nonsmooth-bound asymptotics do not state this explicit rank-policy folded-normal loss law.
